hook: Scammers can now clone a loved one's voice from a short clip.

blocks.narration: Scammers can now clone a loved one's voice from a short clip. Then they call you, pretending that person is in trouble.
blocks.visual: Sleek dark interface with a glowing audio waveform splitting into two identical copies, neon accents

blocks.narration: The Federal Trade Commission has warned about this. AI voice tools can clone how someone sounds from audio posted online.
blocks.visual: Glassy social media panels float by, a waveform being pulled out of a video clip

blocks.narration: The call usually sounds urgent. An accident, an arrest, a stranded trip. And they ask you to keep it secret.
blocks.visual: A phone glows red on a dark table, buzzing urgently

blocks.narration: Then comes the money request, usually something that is hard to reverse, like a wire transfer, gift cards, or cryptocurrency.
blocks.visual: Glowing gift cards and crypto coins spiral toward a dark void

blocks.narration: The fix is surprisingly low tech. Agree on a family safe word that only you know, and ask for it on any emergency call.
blocks.visual: Two hands shake over a glowing padlock icon as a secret word floats between them

blocks.narration: If the caller cannot say it, hang up and call your family member back on a number you already know is real.
blocks.visual: The red phone hangs up and a contact card glows green as a new call begins

blocks.narration: It also helps to set your social profiles to private. Less public audio means less material for scammers to copy.
blocks.visual: A glass panel fades from public to private, the waveform dissolving

blocks.narration: One five-minute conversation at the dinner table can stop this scam cold. Send this to your parents and grandparents tonight.
blocks.visual: A warm family dinner table glows in contrast to the cold neon interface

cta: Send this to your parents tonight.

captions.hook_line: Scammers can clone a loved one's voice from a short clip. Here's the defense 🛑
captions.body: The FTC has warned that scammers use AI voice cloning in family emergency schemes. Agree on a family safe word, hang up and call back on a number you know, and be suspicious of urgent requests for wire transfers, gift cards or crypto.

youtube_title: The AI Voice Scam Targeting Families
